$comment: Pinned download manifest. sha256 values are filled in on first fetch by the fetch scripts and MUST be committed afterwards for integrity checking to mean anything.

win32-x64.note: Filled in on first fetch, then verified on every later fetch.

ytdlp.note: Pinned to an explicit release, not `latest`: this build ships inside the installer, so its digest has to stay meaningful. yt-dlp publishes SHA2-256SUMS; the fetcher prefers that and falls back to pinning locally.

ffmpeg.note: Shipped inside the installer since 0.1.2 (ffmpeg.exe + ffprobe.exe, about 336MB uncompressed). The URL is only used by the optional "download again" action and by npm run fetch:media. It names the `latest` tag rather than going through `releases/latest/download`: that pointer follows whichever release was created most recently, and these builds publish a fresh autobuild every day whose versioned asset names do not include the `master-latest` alias — which is a 404 for the length of that window, and did break a release build once.
